# Assess regulatory approval before a product launch

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before launching a product or business model whose licensing or regulatory classification is uncertain. A qualified market-by-market classification and approval plan with explicit no-launch conditions.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Describe intended use and the complete business model

agent-runnable


Document claims, users, customer types, technology, funds or data handled and target markets. Include physical, health, financial, employment and other high-consequence uses that may change classification.

- Sources: [SBA launch your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/launch-your-business/) · [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Obtain a qualified classification and authority map

human · human approval required


Sector and local counsel identify the competent regulators, product or service classifications and possible exemptions. Record evidence and unresolved questions; a general startup guide cannot approve a clinical, financial or other licensed activity.

- Sources: [SBA launch your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/launch-your-business/) · [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the approval and evidence workplan

agent-runnable


List the specific testing, quality, capital, personnel, documentation and application work identified by specialists. Assign accountable owners, dependencies and expert workstreams rather than estimating permission from a marketing category.

- Sources: [SBA launch your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/launch-your-business/) · [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Authorize specialist submissions and pre-launch controls

human · human approval required


Qualified teams prepare and submit the required applications after proper review and authorization. Record authority decisions and operating restrictions and keep unapproved activities and claims blocked.

- Sources: [SBA launch your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/launch-your-business/) · [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Review the exact permitted launch scope

human · human approval required


The accountable specialists confirm permissions, conditions and operating readiness for each market. Approve only the evidenced scope and establish monitoring and reassessment when the product, claims or business model change.

- Verify: A qualified market-by-market classification and approval plan with explicit no-launch conditions.
- Sources: [SBA launch your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/launch-your-business/) · [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business)
